newsitem.title: USA: Universal Seismic well to be tested.
newsitem.headline: Universal Seismic well to be tested.

text.p: Universal Seismic Associates Inc said Monday completion pipe has been run to total depth of 10,300 feet in the M.W. Petroleum 34 S. Weslaco Gas Unit well in Hidalgo County, Texas.
Significant pay has been calculated in a number of separate sands from 8,730 feet to 10,000 feet and testing is expected to begin this week.

The company owns the well jointly with the operator, an Apache Corp subsidiary after earning an interest in the well and the 6,329 acre acreage block by shooting a 24 square mile proprietary 3-D seismic program in late 1996.
Additional drilling opportunities are currently being evaluated, including development of the field reservoirs and deeper objectives logged as productive in the 34 well.
Universal Seismic also said completion pipe was set to 5,200 feet in the Sandalwood A-6 Welder well in San Patricio County, Texas, where the company owns an approximate 43 percent working interest.
The well encountered a number of productive sands in the Miocene and Frio sections and the operator expects to begin testing the well this week.
Also, the Edge 1 Kolle well in Victoria County, Texas, logged 16 feet of pay from a Frio-age reservoir from 3,746 feet to 3,762 feet.
Universial Seismic owns a 50 percent working interest in the well, an offset to the Edge 1 Hartman well in Victoria County, Texas, which was plugged and abandoned.

The previously announced Talon 1 Newton well, located in Goliad County, Texas, was recently plugged and abaondoned after an unsuccessful completion attempt in Wilcox-age sands. The company owned a 10 percent working interest in the well, which was a carried interest to casing point.
